text: Because higher spectral radius always improves performance, the optimal rho is task-independent and equals exactly 1.0 for every task.
explanation: False: the optimal rho is task-dependent. Tasks with long-range dependencies favor rho near 0.9-0.99, whereas fast-changing / short-memory tasks are best with much smaller rho (e.g. 0.5-0.9). Empirically the NARMA-10 sweep peaks near 0.8-0.95, and performance actually degrades slightly before rho reaches 1, so rho = 1.0 is not a universal optimum.
